I am 66 years old and have been farming these 5 mu in Quzhou since I was 16. After half a century, I know this land and the weather here better than any book. My wife and I are only two people now, so I cannot manage too many crops or waste labor. Cotton has always been my main crop because the soil here suits it and the market in Hebei is steady. This year, I will plant cotton across the whole 5 mu in late April, as soon as the soil warms. I will use an improved variety like guoxinmian or lumianyan — not the expensive hybrid seeds, but the reliable improved ones I have used for years. I will rotary-till the field once to break the winter crust and lay plastic mulch to keep the heat and moisture, which is what everyone here does.

For fertilizer, I will spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as basal dressing, and then top-dress with urea when the cotton starts flowering. I have a well, so I can irrigate three times: once at planting if it is dry, once at flowering in July, and once at boll-setting in August. The well water is reliable, but pumping costs money, so three times is enough. Cotton bollworm is the big enemy here, so I will spray about ten times through the season — I watch the fields myself and spray when I see worms, not by calendar.

For mungbean, I do not need a separate field. In early June, after the cotton is established, I will sow mungbean in the spaces between the cotton rows. This is the old way in our village. The mungbean uses the leftover fertilizer and shares two irrigations with the cotton. It needs almost no extra pesticide because the cotton sprays protect it too. By late July or early August, I can harvest the mungbean before the cotton canopy closes completely. This gives me extra cash and does not cost much labor.

I expect the cotton to yield around 550 jin per mu of seed cotton, which is normal for this land if the weather cooperates. The mungbean should give me about 80 jin per mu from the intercropped strips. I do not chase the highest yield anymore — I chase steady income that two old people can actually bring in.
